messages.subject: Urgent. How does conditional.x work?
parts:
Hello, 

The description of conditional.x is:

If TRUE, we set up the model conditional on the exogenous `x' covariates; the model-implied sample statistics only include the non-x variables. 

This is EXACTLY what I want. But how I do declare the covariates as "x". This may be question about basic R syntax, in which case, I would appreciate a link where I could learn this.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Urgent. How does conditional.x work?
parts:
Any observed variable that is not dependent on any other variable, and whose variance or covariance is not structured or modeled, is a covariate ("x").  So in a model like:
'
F =~ y1 + y2 + y3
F ~ k1
y2 + y3 ~ k2
'
k1 and k2 are covariates. Their position in the model makes them covariates.

messages.subject: Re: Urgent. How does conditional.x work?
parts:
Thanks for the quick response! 

Well, my models works like this:

Half of all my items are reverse coded, and there is a very, very strong measurement artifact (i.e. the usual "reverse-coded item" artifact). So I came up with this idea: 

All observed variables load on two factors: a theoretical factor (one of five theoretically planned factors), and a measurement factor (all reverse coded items have a -1 loading on this one, while all non-reverse coded items have a +1 on this one). Doing this partials out the measurement error, and gives clean factor loadings on the theoretical factors. But the chi square etc, include both factors, I guess. Is there a way by which I could do a chi square ONLY involving the theoretical factors and not the measurement factors?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Urgent. How does conditional.x work?
parts: Is there a way by which I could do a chi square ONLY involving the theoretical factors and not the measurement factors?

No, this is all one model, and this issue has nothing to do with the conditional.x argument.  I think what you want is a bifactor model, where the items load on their trait factor as well as one of two method factors (one for positively worded items and one for negatively worded items), with the trait factor(s) uncorrelated with the method factors.  You should easily find descriptions on Google, but you can ask more questions on the much larger general SEM forum SEMNET:

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Urgent. How does conditional.x work?
parts:
The 'x' in conditional.x (which is only in dev 0.5-21, not official
0.5-20) are observed exogenous variables only.

If you have fitted your model, you can use

lavNames(fit, "ov.x")

to extract those exogenous covariates.

Yves.
